unmapped_findings: The 17Al alloy specific sample aged at 600 °C for 3 h is documented only by Vickers hardness (Table 3: 794.6 ± 58.1 HV) and one SE-SEM panel (Fig. 8, 600 °C-3 h, uniform grey β-Mn matrix); no EBSD, XRD or TEM characterization was performed directly on this exact 600 °C/3 h condition.

For the 17Al alloy the reported β-Mn intrinsic hardness (12.2 ± 0.1 GPa, nanoindentation) and β-Mn composition (Mn 36.2 at.%, Al 16.3 at.%, Cu 2.6 at.%; SEM-EDS) were measured on the hardest sample (575 °C/6 h, 924.9 HV), not on the 600 °C/3 h sample; the peak-hardness 17Al fracture toughness KIC = 6.6 MPa·m1/2 also refers to the 575 °C/6 h sample, so these values are not attributed to this sample.

Aging hardening response of Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels generally slows with increasing Al content; for the 17Al alloy the α→β-Mn transformation is essentially complete after 6 h at 550 °C but after only 1 h at 600 °C and above, consistent with the fully transformed β-Mn matrix observed for this 600 °C/3 h sample.
